home.intro: Fasla is a React component library from Smicolon GmbH, built on shadcn/ui primitives. The CLI copies a component's source into your project — you own it, you edit it, there is no black box to fight.

accessible.title: Accessible by default
accessible.description: Keyboard navigation and screen reader support are built in. Icon-only buttons carry an aria-label; focus styles stay visible.

ownership.title: Yours after install

avatar.fallback: If the photo is missing or fails to load, the avatar shows the initials, or the icon if there's no name.
avatar.lead: A person’s photo, initials or icon, with an optional border and presence dot.
avatar.installNote: The avatar uses status-indicator for its dot, so add both.
avatar.variantsBody: variant picks the content. image, the default, shows the photo, and while it loads or if it fails falls back to initials from name, then to the user icon when there is no name. initials and icon show theirs even when a photo is passed. radius picks a rounded square or a circle, and border adds a ring inside the edge.
avatar.sizesBody: 32 for headers, cards and comments; 24 for dense tables and lists; 12 for inline mentions, where initials shrink to one letter at the 10px XXS size.
avatar.statusBody: status adds a Status Indicator at the end corner — bottom-right, or bottom-left in a right-to-left page. There is no dot unless you set one: it claims the person’s presence, so show it only when you know it.

a11y.name: name names the avatar in every variant: it is the photo’s alt, and hidden text behind the initials or icon, whose visible letters are not read out.
a11y.empty: Pass {emptyName} when a label beside the avatar already names the person, so it isn’t announced twice.
a11y.dot: The dot is read after the name — "Layla Haddad", then "Online", or "متصل" when the nearest lang is Arabic. Pass statusLabel to say more.
a11y.dir: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the dot always sits on the right corner for the page.

usage.circle: Circle with a border and a presence dot
usage.inline: Inline, beside a name that already says who it is

statusIndicator.onAvatar: The dot is meant to sit on an avatar, not on its own over a coloured surface.
statusIndicator.lead: A presence dot — online, away, busy or offline — with an accessible name, so colour never carries the status alone.
statusIndicator.variantsBody: status sets the colour: success for online, warning for away, destructive for busy and muted for offline.
statusIndicator.sizesBody: 8px with a 2px ring, or 4px with a 1px ring for the smallest avatar. The ring is the page background, drawn outside the dot, so it never changes its size.

a11y.colour: Colour alone can’t carry the status. Each dot carries hidden text: "Online", "Away", "Busy" or "Offline", or "متصل", "بعيد", "مشغول" or "غير متصل" when the nearest lang is Arabic. It follows a language change without a reload.
a11y.label: Pass label for more context, such as "Layla is online".
a11y.hidden: When the status is already written next to the dot, hide the dot with aria-hidden so it isn’t announced twice.
a11y.dir: The dot is a circle, so it has no direction. The parent decides where it sits; Avatar pins it to the end corner.

radio.lead: A control for choosing exactly one option from a set.
radio.variantsBody: The layout variant wraps the control and its text in a bordered card, so the whole card becomes the target. Use it when the options carry a description; use the default when they are single words in a tight list.
radio.statesBody: Hover and focus are real CSS states rather than props — hover an option, or tab to it, to see them. Selection is carried by the dot alone; the card chrome does not change.

a11y.nativeInput: Renders a native {input}, so arrow-key navigation and form submission work without extra code.
a11y.group: Options sharing a name form one group, and only one can be selected.
a11y.describedBy: description is linked with aria-describedby; the control graphic is hidden from assistive technology.
a11y.direction: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the control can never disagree with the page.

installation.title: Installation
installation.lead: How to install and set up Fasla in your project.
installation.cliBody: The easiest way to add components is the @smicolon/cli package. It takes two steps.
installation.cliInit: 1. Initialize Fasla, once per project. This writes components.json, which every add reads:
installation.manualBody: You can also copy components directly from the source code.
installation.manualCn: 2. Add the cn utility to your project:
installation.manualCopy: 3. Copy the component source code from each component page.
installation.tailwindBody: Map the semantic tokens into your Tailwind theme. The package exports the whole set, already wrapped so that opacity modifiers keep working:
installation.tailwindNote: Then declare the matching CSS variables as full colours (hex or oklch) on :root and .dark. Mapping a token as a bare var(--primary) looks correct but silently drops Tailwind’s opacity modifiers — bg-primary/10 compiles to no rule at all. That is why the exported map wraps each token in color-mix().

badge.lead: A compact inline label for status, category or metadata, with an optional icon, avatar and close button.
badge.variantsBody: variant sets the visual weight and tone the meaning. Solid is the loudest; Soft lays a tint over the card surface, so it reads the same wherever it sits; Outline is the quietest.
badge.radiusBody: {radiusStandard} swaps the pill for the design system’s small radius.
badge.sizesBody: Heights are minimums: 20, 22 and 26px in English. Arabic’s taller line grows them to 24, 24 and 28px rather than squeezing the text.
badge.statesBody: Pass onClose and the badge gets a real close button. Tab to one to see the focus ring, which wraps the whole badge 2px out.

a11y.span: The badge is a plain {span}. Only the close button is interactive, and it is a native {button}.
a11y.closeName: The close button is named after the label, "Remove Cairo", or "إزالة القاهرة" when the nearest lang is Arabic. It follows a language change without a reload. Pass closeLabel for more context, such as "Remove filter: Cairo".
a11y.icon: The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. The avatar is not: give the Avatar a name, or {emptyName} when the label already names the person.
a11y.tone: Don’t rely on tone alone to carry meaning — the label should say it.
a11y.dir: Direction is inherited from dir, never a prop, so the badge can never disagree with the page.
